newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Five killed in SAfrican political attack.
newsitem.headline: Five killed in SAfrican political attack.

text.p: Five people, including two recently elected African National Council (ANC) councillors, were shot dead in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province in a political attack, police said on Wednesday.
The bodies were found by police near Richmond in central KwaZulu-Natal province, where a by-election was held on Sunday.
"We found five bodies this morning (Wednesday).... They sustained gunshot wounds to the head. It appears the attack was politically motivated," Superintendent Henry Budhram told Reuters.
ANC mayor Andrew Ragavaloo told a local radio station the five had been killed in execution style.
The area has been identified as a hotspot by violence monitors after ANC leader Sifiso Nkabinde was thrown out of the party earlier this year on allegations of spying for the former white government.

His expulsion was followed by the resignation of a group of ANC councillors who wanted to show their support for Nkabinde, a self-confessed warlord. Another councillor, deputy mayor Rodney van der Byl, refused to resign and was shot dead at his home soon after.
Nkabinde has joined former ANC member Bantu Holomisa's newly formed National Consultative Forum (NCF). Holomisa was also expelled from the ANC.
The ANC won four of the five wards in Richmond with significant majorities. The NCF won one ward.
